title: Minimum Time Difference
statement:
Every string in `timePoints` is a time of day on a 24-hour clock, written as `"HH:MM"` (anything from `"00:00"` to `"23:59"`). Return the smallest gap, in minutes, between two entries at different positions of the list.

- The clock wraps at midnight, so the gap between two times is measured the shorter way around the 1440-minute day: `"23:59"` and `"00:00"` are 1 minute apart.
- The same time listed twice gives a gap of 0.
constraints: Each timePoints[i] has the form "HH:MM" with 00 <= HH <= 23 and 00 <= MM <= 59
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every pair of times works in O(n²). But once the times are turned into minutes after midnight and sorted, the closest pair must sit next to each other in the sorted list, because any time between two others is nearer to both of them. The one extra pair to check is the wrap across midnight: the latest time and the earliest time, which are `first + 1440 - last` minutes apart.

## Approach

1. Convert each `"HH:MM"` into `hours * 60 + mins` and collect the values in `minutes`.
2. Sort `minutes` in ascending numeric order.
3. Start `best` at the midnight gap: `minutes[0] + 1440 - minutes[minutes.length - 1]`.
4. Scan neighbours `minutes[i - 1]` and `minutes[i]`, keeping the smallest difference in `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`"23:59"` becomes 1439 and `"00:00"` becomes 0, so the sorted `minutes` is `[0, 1439]`. The midnight gap is `0 + 1440 - 1439 = 1`, so `best = 1`. The only neighbouring pair differs by 1439, which does not improve it, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) to sort; converting and scanning are O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `minutes`.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the wrap-around pair gives 1439 instead of 1 for `["23:59", "00:00"]`.
- Sort numbers with a comparator; the default JavaScript sort orders them as text.
- With more than 1440 entries two must be equal (pigeonhole), so the answer is 0; a counting array of 1440 slots can exploit this to avoid sorting.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `minutes` | each time as minutes after midnight, later sorted |
| `hours`, `mins` | the two parts of one `"HH:MM"` string |
| `best` | smallest gap found so far |
| `i` | index of the right element of the neighbouring pair |

narration.3: Look at each time string in turn.
narration.4: The two characters before the colon are the hours.
narration.5: The two characters after the colon are the minutes.
narration.6: Store the time as minutes after midnight.
narration.8: Sort so that the closest times end up next to each other.
narration.10: The pair across midnight: the earliest time plus a full day, minus the latest.
narration.11: Walk through every neighbouring pair in sorted order.
narration.12: Keep the smaller of the best so far and this pair's gap.
narration.14: The smallest gap over all neighbours and the wrap is the answer.
